newsitem.title: USA: Seven arrested at Wall Street protest.
newsitem.headline: Seven arrested at Wall Street protest.

text.p: Seven persons were arrested by police at a demonstration at a Wall Street protest by AIDS activists, a group spokesman said.

Police were not immediately able to confirm the number of those arrested but confirmed there were arrests. The protestors of the activist group Act Up were arrested as they tried to climb police barracades about a block from the New York Stock Exchange.
More than 200 persons chanting "Fight AIDS," "Act Up," and "Fight" and carrying placards saying "AIDS Drugs: Your Money or Your Life" marched down Broadway, slowing traffic.
The number of arrested AIDS activists at the Wall Street protest against the high price of AIDS drugs rose to 55 later Monday morning, according to a police spokesman at the scene.
Louis Anemone, Chief of Department of the New York City police, said most of those arrested would be charged with disorderly conduct.

Anemone said most of those arrested had sat down on the sidewalk and refused police orders to move. A handful of others were arrested for throwing an unidentified liquid at the New York Stock Exchange and one for apparently kicking a polce officer.

More than 200 protestors from the group Act Up chanted "Fight AIDS, Act Up, Fight Back" in front of the New York Stock Exchange. Several dozen police officers, some on motor scooters, kept the protestors across Broad Street from the exchange.
NYSE Chairman Richard Grasso came out of the exchange briefly around the time trading began.
"This is America," Grasso said to a reporter. "People are free to speak their piece." Grasso conferred briefly with top police officials them went back into the exchange building.
Act Up spokesman said they chose the exchange as the site for their protest because it symbolized the heart of corporate America.
They were protesting against pharmaceutical companies that they claim charge exorbitant prices for AIDS drugs.

Earlier, police blocked off several streets around the exchange, allowing only people who work in the immediate area to proceed past the barricades. The police check managed create a bottleneck for workers beyond the barricades as police checked worker identifications.
An exchange spokesman said the market would open at the normal 0930 EST (1430 GMT).
